title: PACE shows that KV-cache retention alone can fail on long-horizon agent tasks
summary: Experiments on long-horizon LLM-agent tasks found that retaining apparently relevant key-value cache tokens alone did not reliably support later task completion. PACE combines retention decisions with rehydration controls and is evaluated with component ablations and fresh tasks. The result is limited to the paper’s task suite and agent setup.
ai_technology: PACE plan-aware KV-cache retention and tiered rehydration

evidence.tested: The study compares retention-only strategies with PACE, which combines plan-aware retention and rehydration; preregistered fresh tasks and ablations assess long-horizon outcomes.
evidence.unknown: The evidence is limited to the evaluated tasks and agent setup; it does not establish performance across all long-horizon workloads.
evidence.ai_role: PACE uses plan-aware cache retention and rehydrates evicted context when later steps require it.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
